6.evidence_source: Following best-practice recommendations for the test adaptation of body image instruments (Swami & Barron, 2018), we translated the BAS-2 from English to Malay using the five-stage procedure proposed by Beaton, Bombardier, Guillemin, and Ferraz, (2000).
6._section_summary: This section describes the five-stage Beaton et al. (2000) translation and adaptation procedure used to translate the BAS-2 into Malay, including forward/back translations, committee review, and minor item revisions. It reports a pre-test of the prefinal Malay BAS-2 in a sample of 40 Malay-fluent individuals (women = 60.0%), with mean item understanding overall M = 3.98 (SD = 0.46) and four items with Ms < 4.0 returned for further revision.

7.evidence_source: Text: "To examine the factor structure of Malay BAS-2 scores..." and "Our plan was to examine fit of the one-factor model of BAS-2 scores..."
7._section_summary: This analytic strategy describes a two-step EFA-to-CFA approach applied to Malay and Chinese participants: the Malay sample was split into two halves (EFA: women n = 149, men n = 157; CFA: Malay women n = 121, Malay men n = 114) and the CFA half was combined with Chinese participants (women n = 120, men n = 120) yielding n = 475 for CFA. Missing data (1.1%) were multiply imputed; EFA was conducted separately by sex and CFA used robust maximum likelihood with Satorra-Bentler correction, plus tests of measurement invariance and assessments of reliability and convergent/incremental validity.

8.evidence_source: "For the Malay female subsample (n = 149), Bartlett's test ... indicated that the BAS-2 items had adequate common variance for factor analysis." Also: "For the Malay male subsample (n=157), Bartlett's test ... again indicated that the BAS-2 items had adequate common variance for factor analysis."
8._section_summary: This section reports exploratory factor analyses of the BAS-2 for Malay female (n = 149) and Malay male (n = 157) subsamples. Parallel analysis indicated a single factor for the female subsample (first eigenvalue 5.45 > random 3.28) explaining 54.5% of variance and a single factor for the male subsample (eigenvalue 4.98) explaining 49.83% of variance; omega for the 10-item BAS-2 was .88 in both subsamples. Tucker's congruence coefficient = .85 suggests similar but not identical factor structures across the two subsamples.

9.evidence_source: In the second split-half subsample (n=475), we examined the fit of a one-factor model of BAS-2 scores.
9._section_summary: This section reports a confirmatory factor analysis conducted in the second split-half subsample (n=475), testing a one-factor model of BAS-2 scores with initial poor fit (e.g., robust RMSEA = .103). After freeing specified error covariances (Items 6&7, 1&6, 3&4) model fit improved (robust RMSEA = .080), with omega = .88 and AVE = .57 indicating acceptable reliability and convergent validity.

10.evidence_source: We, therefore, computed a 2 \times 2 ANOVA with sex and ethnicity as the independent factors and BAS-2 scores as the dependent variable.
10._section_summary: This section reports measurement invariance tests of the BAS-2 across sex and between Malay and Chinese participants, finding configural and metric but only partial scalar invariance after freeing specific items. A 2 x 2 ANOVA on BAS-2 scores (Note. N = 781) found no Sex or Sex x Ethnicity interaction, but a significant Ethnicity main effect with Malay participants (M = 4.17, SD = 0.60) scoring higher than Chinese participants (M = 3.88, SD = 0.59).

14.evidence_source: We examined the construct validity of BAS-2 scores through associations with scores on additional measures included in the present study and using the total sample (with analyses conducted separately for women and men).
14._section_summary: This section reports construct and incremental validity analyses for BAS-2 scores conducted on the present study's total sample, with analyses run separately for women and men. It states that body appreciation in women was negatively associated with BMI (significant), whereas the association with BMI in men did not reach significance; hierarchical regressions showed BAS-2 provided incremental prediction of subjective happiness in both women and men.

15.evidence_source: In the present study, we examined the factor structure and psychometric properties of a Malay translation of the BAS-2.
15._section_summary: This Discussion summarizes psychometric evaluation of a Malay translation of the BAS-2 in a Malaysian community sample, reporting a one-dimensional factor structure supported by EFA and CFA, adequate internal consistency (omega ≥ .88), and partial invariance across sex and ethnicity. It notes that body appreciation related positively to life satisfaction and subjective happiness, showed equivocal associations with BMI (significant in women but not men), and highlights strengths (translation process, community sample) and limitations (opportunistic recruitment, limited ethnic coverage, lack of test-retest).

1._section_summary: This introduction reviews the development and validation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its refinement, the BAS-2, across many countries and sample types. It highlights evidence for one-dimensional BAS-2 structure in many validations, discusses mixed findings regarding sex invariance and sex differences, and notes inconsistent associations between BAS-2 scores and BMI across studies.
